title: Leave the consequences hidden
hook: Would you pay attention to how your choice affects the other player?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish choosing under ignorance from choosing after learning the consequence.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish choosing under ignorance from choosing after learning the consequence.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy recipient gets either two or eight units with equal probability, while the chooser has not learned which. What is the expected recipient payoff? Toy inputs A=[2, 8, 0.5]; B=[8, 8, 1].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[5, 2, 8], [8, 8, 8]]. Labels: Expected payoff, Low, High.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Hidden consequences leave a range of possible recipient outcomes. Revealing a specific outcome changes information, even if the chooser’s own payment is fixed. The expected value is not a guarantee or a diagnosis of fairness.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Outcome 1=8, Outcome 2=8, P(outcome 1)=1. What is Expected payoff? Answer: 8.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Outcome 1=8, Outcome 2=8, P(outcome 1)=1. What is Expected payoff?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 8. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: When people could avoid learning how their choice affected others, fair choices roughly halved (Dana, Weber & Kuang, 2007).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish choosing under ignorance from choosing after learning the consequence.
